messages:
maria: Heads up — p95s in dublin-pop just jumped ~3.5x after the kernel-opt rollout a few minutes ago. Noticing both higher latencies and throughput drop. :eyes:

deploy-bot: Deploy finished: infra/kernel-opt v2.3 -> dublin-pop at 2026-03-10T08:20Z (canary 10%, then full).

aj: Confirming. p95 went from ~120ms -> ~420ms, p99 up too. RPS at the edge is down ~22%.

kai: Any signs of network flaps? traceroutes look stable. My hunch: IO or scheduler interactions with the new kernel patch.

oliver: I grabbed a quick perf during a spike window — see below (sampled stacks, condensed):

```
# perf top snapshot
  18.4%  inference_runtime  [kernel.kallsyms]
  12.1%  inference_runtime  kv_cache_lookup
   9.3%  libc-2.35.so       futex_wait
   8.7%  inference_runtime  batch_router::route
   7.2%  kernel             __do_softirq
```

oliver: Notice the sys/kernel softirq and futex wait time — threads are getting stuck waiting on IO/locks, which amplifies latency when batching peaks.

nina: Metrics: kvcache.evictions/sec spiked 3x at the same time, kvcache.hit_rate dropped from 0.91 -> 0.65. KV cache size unchanged.

kajustkidding: (sorry wrong channel)

kai: Copying some commands I ran: 
`iostat -x 1 5` showed nvme0n1 util ~98% during the window. `dmesg | tail -n 50` had scattered ATA timeouts on host 10.10.4.22.

aj: So noisy-disk on a colocated instance causing IO saturation -> KV cache evictions -> more misses -> more disk access -> event loop stalls -> batching heuristic triggers larger batches -> higher p95. That feedback loop fits observed shape.

maria: Interesting — the kernel-opt v2.3 changed IRQ/softirq processing path (optimizes for throughput) which may make the runtime less resilient to high device latency. Could be flipping kernel selection into a code path that assumes fast IO.

oliver: Also saw our runtime switch from the 'fast-kernels' path to the fallback 'generic-kernels' during the spike (logs: `kernel_select: fallback to generic-kernel (reason=io-delay-threshold)`). That matches a perf hit.

sre-bot: Alert: POP dublin-pop experiencing sustained p95 > 300ms for ~8m. Ticket infra#11456 auto-created.

nina: Short-term mitigations: 1) throttle batch size on dublin route to 1.5x smaller, 2) pin model instances away from noisy hosts via placement tags, 3) throttle unrelated jobs on same hosts.

kai: I can try a quick rollback of kernel-opt to v2.2 for the pop (canary then full) — that'll test if the kernel change amplified the problem.

aj: Also recommend enabling NVMe IO QOS for the guest to limit noisy neighbor impact while we investigate.

maria: Agreed. Rollback is safest immediate test. I'll coordinate with infra to start a rollback canary (2 nodes) now. If p95 returns to baseline -> we confirm regression tied to kernel-opt + IO saturation interaction.

oliver: I'll capture a full flame and perf.data for the rollback window and annotate logs with `kernel_select` events.

maria: Rollback to v2.2 started (canary nodes). Will report back in ~5m. :white_check_mark:

aj: Thanks — also creating a short playbook note so oncall knows to reduce batch config and check `iostat` + `kvcache.*` metrics during spikes.

maria: Final note: this one looks like an incident born from a combination of kernel scheduling changes + noisy-disk. Not just routing or DNS. We'll follow up with a postmortem if rollback confirms.

maria: (update) Canary rollback completed — canary p95 back to ~130ms after ~3m. Rolling full rollback now.

nina: Great, I'll keep an eye on evictions and hit rate.

maria: Closing loop: rollback finished, metrics trending back to normal. Filing follow-up RFC to add IO QOS + test case for kopt changes.
